title: Franchising Microfinance
abstract: Abstract Financial intermediaries worldwide are seeking mechanisms for participating in micro lending. Using informed “local capitalists” as bank's on-lenders fails due to borrowers' incentive to default with multiple credit sources. A coalition of local capitalists may not resolve the problem in the presence of a monopoly moneylender with superior skills in lending and enforcement. A credible competitive threat to the moneylender can only arise if the local capitalist coalition also provides information sharing benefits that lower their cost of lending vis-à-vis the moneylender. Franchising allows local capitalists to form such a coalition. We analyze conditions under which welfare-enhancing franchising would obtain.

summary.oneLiner: Franchising lets local capitalists form a coalition that shares information and cuts lending costs, creating a credible threat to a monopoly moneylender in micro lending.
summary.overview: Banks worldwide want ways to take part in micro lending, but using local capitalists as on-lenders is hard because borrowers may default by taking loans from several sources. The paper argues that a group of local lenders working together may not solve this when a single moneylender has better lending and enforcement skills. A credible competitive threat arises only if the coalition also shares information that lowers its lending costs relative to the moneylender. The authors argue that franchising is a way for local capitalists to form such a coalition, and they analyze when this franchising would improve welfare.
summary.question: Can franchising allow local capitalists to form a coalition that competes with a monopoly moneylender in micro lending, and under what conditions would this be welfare-enhancing?
summary.method: Theoretical analysis; the abstract describes analyzing conditions under which the arrangement would obtain but does not name the specific modelling approach.

findings: Using informed local capitalists as on-lenders for a bank fails because borrowers have an incentive to default when they can borrow from multiple credit sources.
A coalition of local capitalists may not resolve this problem when a monopoly moneylender has superior lending and enforcement skills.

A credible competitive threat to the moneylender can arise only if the local capitalist coalition also provides information sharing benefits that lower its cost of lending relative to the moneylender.
Franchising allows local capitalists to form such a coalition.
The authors analyze conditions under which welfare-enhancing franchising would obtain.
summary.whyItMatters: The paper suggests that financial intermediaries seeking to enter micro lending may use franchising, with local capitalists as franchisees sharing information, as a mechanism to compete with an entrenched local moneylender. The abstract frames the result in terms of welfare gains under certain conditions.
